subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statements :
stem: The arts of painting and sculpting are ____.
solution: **(A)** Visual arts. Artistic creations are of two types, visual arts (Drik Kala) and performing arts (Lalit or Aangik Kala). Painting and sculpting create a work that is seen, so they are visual arts. Folk art and classical art are two traditions of art, not the type to which painting and sculpting belong.

subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statements :
stem: The first English newspaper in India was started by ____.
solution: **(A)** James Augustus Hickey. The first English newspaper in India was started in January 1780 and was named the 'Calcutta General Advertiser' or 'Bengal Gazette'. It was started by James Augustus Hickey, an Irish gentleman. Balshastri Jambhekar was the editor of 'Darpan', the newspaper started in Mumbai in 1832.

subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statements :
stem: The Museum named, ____ at Kolkata is the first museum in India.
solution: **(D)** Indian Museum. The first museum in India, the 'Indian Museum', was established by the Asiatic Society of Bengal in Kolkata in 1814 C.E. The Government Museum at Chennai (1851 C.E.) was the second museum in India, and the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastusangrahalay is in Mumbai.

subject: History
context: Write short notes (any two) :
stem: Write a short note on: Saraswati Mahal Library.
solution: The 'Saraswati Mahal Granthalay' is at Thanjavur in Tamilnadu. It was built in the 16th-17th century, during the times of the Nayak dynasty. In 1675 C.E. Vyankojiraje Bhosale conquered Thanjavur and established his independent rule there. Vyankojiraje Bhosale and his successors kept expanding the Saraswati Mahal Granthalay, and Sarfojiraje Bhosale contributed the most to this expansion. In 1918 the library was renamed 'The Thanjavur Maharaja Sarfoji's Saraswati Mahal Library' in his honour. It is one of the noteworthy libraries of India.

subject: History
context: Write short notes (any two) :
stem: Write a short note on: Agro-tourism.
solution: Agro-tourism is one of the types of tourism, along with religious, historical, health, science and sports tourism. It is also known as agri-tourism. It is developing rapidly and is meant especially for the urban population, which has very little exposure to rural life and agriculture; through it they get to see and experience life in the villages and on the farms. Indian farmers also take part in this kind of tourism: they now visit faraway places like agricultural research centres, agricultural universities and countries like Israel, where experiments in the advanced technology of agriculture are carried out. In this way agro-tourism spreads knowledge of agriculture and links the city with the village.

subject: History
context: Write short notes (any two) :
stem: Write a short note on: Annales School.
solution: At the onset of the twentieth century a new school of historiography arose in France, which is known as the 'Annales School'. It was started by French historians. The Annales School gave a new direction to history writing. Before it, history was mainly about political events, kings, great leaders, politics, diplomacy and wars. The Annales School established that history is also about the climate, the local people, agriculture, trade, technology, the means of communication, social divisions and the collective psychology of people in historical times. In this way it widened the scope of history to include the whole life of society.

subject: History
context: Explain the following statements with reasons (any two) :
stem: Knowledge of history is essential for newspaper articles.
solution: Newspapers have to give fresh news to their readers and also unfold the background of an event in the news, and for this they have to resort to history. While reporting news in detail, reporters compare it with parallel events which happened in the past, and such a past event is often printed in a separate frame, so the reader gets better insight into the current news. Newspapers print columns such as '50 Years Ago' or '100 Years Ago', which are based on historical documents or written history. They also publish supplements and special issues on anniversaries, for example on the 100th year of World War I in 2014 and on 75 years of the 'Quit India' movement in 2017, with articles, editorials and columns like 'what happened in history on this day'. Therefore knowledge of history is essential for newspaper articles.

subject: History
context: Explain the following statements with reasons (any two) :
stem: Currently the structure of sports economy has been significantly affected.
solution: In the 20th-21st century the field of sports was influenced by the process of globalisation. International matches of cricket, football, lawn tennis and other sports can now be watched on television in any corner of the world, so even citizens of countries that are not playing can enjoy them; the world cup winning match of the Indian cricketers was watched by fans all over the world. Fans watch these matches for entertainment, industrial and commercial companies use them as a good opportunity to advertise their goods, and retired sportsmen get an opportunity to work as commentators. Thus sports fans scattered all over the world have significantly affected the entire structure of the sports economy has been significantly affected.

subject: History
subtopic: Conservation and Preservation of Historical Places
context: Explain the following statements with reasons (any two) :
stem: It is important to take a few primary precautions in order to preserve the natural and cultural heritage sites.
solution: It is a hard task to preserve and conserve heritage sites, and India is rich in historical sites of the ancient, medieval and modern periods as well as in natural heritage like the Kas plateau in the Western Ghats. At many such sites people write their names with charcoal, draw pictures, carve on trees and paint ancient monuments in garish colours, which vandalises and defaces them and affects our image as a nation. Lack of good amenities in the precincts of a heritage site also causes filthiness. Therefore a few primary precautions are needed: everybody should avoid writing on walls or carving on trees, nobody should do anything that vandalises a historical site, and every visitor should help to keep the site clean. Only by taking such precautions can the natural and cultural heritage sites be preserved for the future.

subject: History
context: Explain the following statements with reasons (any two) :
stem: Writing of the regional history received a momentum.
solution: British officers had written a prejudiced history of India. Indian historians trained in the British educational system wrote nationalistic history to restore pride in India's past and the self-esteem of Indian readers. This nationalistic historiography provided a momentum to the writing of regional histories, and the attention of historians was drawn to the geographic conditions and history of the south Indian regions. In Maharashtra, V.K. Rajwade held that we should write our own history from authentic documentary sources and compiled 22 volumes of 'Marathyanchya Itihasachi Sadhane', and Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade explained the background of the rise of the Maratha empire in 'The Rise of Maratha Power'. Hence the writing of regional history received a momentum.

context:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it :

Temples in Maharashtra built in 12th-13th centuries are known as Hemadpanti temples. The outer walls of Hemadpanti temples are built in a star shape. In the star-shaped plan, the outer walls of the temple has a zigzag design. This results into an interesting effect of alternating light and shadow. The important characteristic of Hemadpanti temple is its masonry. The walls are built without using any mortar, by locking the stones by using the technique of tenon and mortise joints. The Ambreshwar temple at Ambarnath near Mumbai, Gondeshwar temple at Sinnar near Nashik, Aundha Nagnath temple in the Hingoli district are a few finest examples of the Hemadpanti style. Their plan is star-shaped. The Hemadpanti temples are found at several places in Maharashtra.
stem: In which state do we find the Hemadpanti temples ?
solution: We find the Hemadpanti temples in Maharashtra.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Explain Karl Marx's 'Class Theory'.
solution:
In the latter half of the nineteenth century a new school of thought arose from the thesis formulated by Karl Marx (1818-1883). His Class Theory may be explained as follows:
(1) According to Marx, history is not about abstract ideas; it is about living people.
(2) Human relationships are shaped by the fundamental needs of people and by the ownership and nature of the means of production that meet those needs.
(3) The access of the different strata of society to these means of production is not equal.
(4) This inequality divides society into classes, and the division leads to class struggle. The class that owns the means of production economically exploits the rest of the classes.
(5) Therefore, according to Marx, human history is the history of class struggle.
His treatise 'Das Kapital' is the most referred book all over the world. His theory gave rise to Marxist historiography, which studies the means and modes of production and industrial relations; in India, Marxist historians like Damodar Dharmanand Kosambi and Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange studied the transitions within the caste system from this point of view.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: How can we correlate applied history with our present ?
solution:
Applied history, also known as public history, is the application of history for the benefit of people in the present and the future. We can correlate it with our present as follows:
(1) The visible and invisible relics of the past exist in the present. They represent the creative thoughts and traditions of our ancestors; this is our heritage, it builds our identity and links us with our origin.
(2) Applied history is concerned with the preservation and conservation of this heritage and with making it accessible to people, for our benefit and for the benefit of future generations.
(3) Knowledge of history can guide us in finding solutions to contemporary social issues and in social planning.
(4) People can take part in such projects as tourists visiting museums and ancient sites, and as volunteers in the conservation projects of their own city, town or village.
(5) Heritage management creates opportunities of employment in fields like museums, archives, tourism and mass media.
In brief, applied history means understanding our present with the help of history and finding the right direction for the benefit of our future.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: What is Powada ?
solution:
Powada (ballad) is a form of folk theatre of Maharashtra.
(1) It is a dramatic narration in which poetry and prose extracts are recited alternately.
(2) A Powada narrates the great deeds of heroic men and women in a very forceful and inspiring style.
(3) The Powada composed by Adnyandas, a contemporary poet of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, on the killing of Afzal Khan, and the Powada on the battle of Sinhagad composed by Tulasidas are two well-known examples.
(4) In the British period, Powadas narrating the stories of Umaji Naik, the Chapekar brothers and Mahatma Gandhi were composed.
(5) During the 'Samyukt Maharashtra' movement, Powadas were used as a medium of creating public awareness.
Thus the Powada is a lively folk art that keeps the memory of heroic deeds alive and inspires the people.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Write down the history of television.
solution:
Television is an audio-visual medium. It crossed the limitations of newspapers and the radio and could show people the actual visuals of an event. Its history in India is as follows:
(1) The 'Delhi Doordarshan Centre' was inaugurated by Dr Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, on 15th September 1959.
(2) Doordarshan's Mumbai centre began to telecast its programmes on 1st May 1972.
(3) Colour television was introduced on 15th August 1982.
(4) In 1991 the Government of India granted permission to private national and international channels to telecast in India, and it became possible for Indians to watch international events on television.
(5) Doordarshan and other channels created interest in history through serials like 'Ramayana', 'Mahabharata', 'Bharat Ek Khoj' and 'Raja Shivchhatrapati'. 'Bharat Ek Khoj', directed by Shyam Benegal, was based on Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru's book 'Discovery of India'.
(6) Today channels like 'Discovery', 'National Geographic' and 'History' have opened a rich treasure of global history for the audience at home.

subject: Political Science
stem: In Maharashtra, ____ seats are reserved for women in local self-governing institutions.
solution: **(D)** 50%. The 73rd and 74th amendments to the Constitution reserved 33% of the seats for women in local self-governing institutions. This percentage has been raised to 50% in several states, including Maharashtra, to increase the political participation of women.

subject: Political Science
subtopic: Characteristics and Functions of Political Parties
stem: In a democracy ____ participate in elections and get political power.
solution: **(A)** Political parties. When people form organisations with the objective of achieving political power and take part in the electoral process, such organisations are called political parties. They contest elections, win them, get power and establish the government of their party. Social organisations and non-government organisations work for social causes without contesting elections, and courts settle disputes.

subject: Political Science
setLabel: Q7 True or false with reasons
context: State whether the following statements are true or false. Give reasons for your answers (any two) :
stem: Secrecy in the working of Government has increased due to the Right to Information.
solution: False. Citizens have a right to know about the functioning of the government. The Government of India gave the Right to Information (RTI 2005) to citizens to ensure transparency and accountability, which are the hallmarks of good governance. Under it any citizen can seek information about the working of the government. Thus the Right to Information has made the government more transparent and has reduced, not increased, the element of secrecy in its working.

subject: Political Science
setLabel: Q7 True or false with reasons
context: State whether the following statements are true or false. Give reasons for your answers (any two) :
stem: The Election Commission lays down the Code of Conduct during elections.
solution: True. To ensure free and fair elections in India, the Election Commission has adopted several measures, and the Code of Conduct is one of them. It lays down the rules to be followed by the government, the political parties and the voters before and during the elections. Even the government cannot violate these rules; the government has to observe the code of conduct declared by the Election Commission. Due to its strict observance in the last few elections, common voters have become confident.

subject: Political Science
setLabel: Q7 True or false with reasons
context: State whether the following statements are true or false. Give reasons for your answers (any two) :
stem: Movements are important in a democracy.
solution: True. All the people in society cannot participate in political parties. Some people take up a particular issue, organise people, build public opinion and put pressure on the political parties and the government to resolve it; such organised activity is a movement. Through movements, social problems come up for discussion and the government has to pay attention to them, and the information given by the leaders and activists is useful to the government in making policies. Movements also increase the participation of people in public life. Hence movements are important in a democracy.

subject: Political Science
context: Explain the following concepts (any one) :
stem: Regionalism
solution: In India people speak different languages and have different traditions and cultures in different regions. The feeling of affinity for one's own language and region gradually turns into identity consciousness and finally gives rise to regionalism. People start thinking primarily about the interest and development of their own region and feel that the people of the region should have a claim over its resources and employment opportunities. When linguistic, regional and cultural identities get connected, this regional consciousness becomes stronger, and sometimes it gives rise to regional political parties, pressure groups or movements that aim at protecting the interests of the region.

subject: Political Science
context: Explain the following concepts (any one) :
stem: Left-extremism.
solution: Left-extremism in India is known as Naxalism, and it is a major problem before Indian democracy. Naxalism began as a movement to remove the injustice done to landless farmers and tribal people. Today, however, it has become a violent struggle. In the Naxalite movement the importance of the problems of farmers and tribal people has reduced; instead, Naxalite groups use violent means to oppose government policies, such as attacking the police forces. Because it relies on violence rather than democratic means, left-extremism is a challenge to Indian democracy.

subject: Political Science
context: Answer in brief (any one) :
stem: Write some additional information about the post of the Election Commissioner.
solution: The Election Commission of India is an autonomous body established by Article 324 of the Constitution. It consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two other Election Commissioners, who are appointed by the President. The Chief Election Commissioner cannot be removed from his post easily or on account of any political reasons; this is necessary to preserve the independence of the Election Commission. There is a separate provision for the expenses of the Commission, and it has no separate staff of its own: government officers, teachers and other employees help it to conduct elections. Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner after independence; he took charge after the Election Commission was established in 1950.

subject: Political Science
subtopic: Characteristics and Functions of Political Parties
context: Answer in brief (any one) :
stem: What are the major characteristics of political parties ?
solution:
The major characteristics of political parties are:
(1) To be in power: achieving power through elections is the main objective of political parties, so they compete with each other, and the competition should be fair.
(2) To pursue an ideology: every party has its own policies, world view and stand on social issues, and the people who accept its ideology form its mass base.
(3) To have a party agenda: parties prepare an agenda on the basis of their ideology and implement it when they get power.
(4) To establish a government: the party that gets a majority forms the government, and the others act as opposition parties.
(5) To act as a link between the government and the people: parties carry the demands and complaints of the people to the government, and the government gets the people's support for its policies through them.
